subject: Interface mapping & rollout validation plan for Aurelia migration
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@aurelia-health.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aurelia-health.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Implementation detail request — interface mapping & canary validation

Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to consolidate a detailed plan and a validation matrix we can include in the RFP response — specifically:

- Full list of endpoints/interfaces we need to integrate (auth, logging, telem)
- Data flows for PHI handling (at-rest/in-transit, KMS)
- Canary rollout gating criteria and automated rollback triggers
- Estimated timeline by milestone (staging, canary, full cutover)

Can you share a proposed integration timeline and the validation checklist you run during canary? If you can also include any network/firewall requirements and an SOW sign-off link, that would speed internal approvals.

I can route this to our engineering ops and procurement as soon as we have it.

Appreciate it,
Daniel
Daniel Cho
Director, Clinical IT Programs
Aurelia Health Systems

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: procurement@aurelia-health.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Implementation detail request — interface mapping & canary validation

Daniel —

Attached is a first-pass integration & validation package: 'redwood_interface_mapping_v1.xlsx' (interface inventory + staged validation checklist) and a short network topology summary 'network_topology_ascii.pdf'. High level notes below:

- Milestones (estimated):
  * Week 0: Kickoff & environment setup (VPC peering, KMS onboarding)
  * Week 1–2: Staging integration — API keys, auth flow, embed tests
  * Week 3: Canary (5% traffic) + automated quality gates for latency, error-rate, and hallucination regression on golden prompts
  * Week 4: Expand canary to 25% with sustained SLOs; finalize runbook and rollback windows
  * Week 5: Full cutover and 2-week hypercare

- Canary gating criteria (short):
  * 95th pct latency <= 300ms (internal infra SLO)
  * Error rate < 0.5% for tokenization/serving errors
  * Quality regression: no >5% drop in golden set pass rate (we'll supply the eval harness)
  * KV cache hit rate stable (to avoid cost spikes)

- Network / firewall: TLS 1.2+, outbound to redwood egress IP range (see attachment), TLS client cert optional for private deploys. Ports: 443 + 5222 for internal websockets.

I'm looping in Laura and Rishi for canary/runbook specifics and security sign-off. Also included a DocuSign link below; if procurement approves the SOW we can kick off next Monday.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/instance/ABC-12345
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/DEAL-2026-089

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Implementation detail request — interface mapping & canary validation

Karthik / Laura —

Quick notes after a pass through the matrix:

- Network egress: we'll provide a CIDR block list (10 IPs) for staged peering; require company firewall to allow outbound to those IPs on 443 only. For private deployments we recommend TLS+mutual auth (mTLS).
- Monitoring: add GPU mem pressure and queue depth metrics to the canary dashboard; alert if GPU queue depth > 70% for more than 3 consecutive minutes.
- Canary duration: change Week 3 to a two-week rolling canary (day-2 evaluation windows) for healthcare customers — heals issues faster and gives ops time to collect quality metrics.
- Rollback: automated rollback triggers on: tokenization errors >0.5% OR service error rate spike >1% OR golden set quality drop >6% within a 2-hour window. Manual rollback still requires Eng lead approval in the first canary week.

I've attached a short note in the spreadsheet with the updated gating thresholds. Laura — please add the escalation matrix.

-rishi
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
